rv.q: But the show is let down by an uncertainty (of tone, of characterisation) that hovers, sometimes distractingly, over everything.
It should surely be an even better production now that it is so timely, but somehow isn't.
Yet no such vital sense of things fundamentally mattering is forthcoming in Rachel O’Riordan’s stilted revival.

Although King is a master of her craft, this production of Foxfinder does somewhat miss the mark. Greeted by Gary McCann's superb set design, a house of Scandinavian simplicity that bleeds into a dark forest with towering trees and realistic dirt mounds, husband and wife Samuel (Paul Nicholls) and Judith (Heida Reed) Covey await the arrival of a...

Foxfinder was originally seen in 2011 in a tiny, but hugely acclaimed, production at the Finborough Theatre, directed by Blanche McIntyre. For that production the author, Dawn King, won the Theatre Foundation Playwright award, the Most Promising Playwright at the Off Awards and was shortlisted for Best New Play at the Off Awards.

cn.t: Dawn King's dystopian thriller receives a lukewarm West End transfer, with critics finding the 2011 play's allegorical premise intriguing but the production failing to capture the alchemy that made the original fringe run a success.
